title: Customer Support Automation Platform: 2026 Guide
summary: A customer support automation platform comparison helps you choose between Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk and other tools based on your needs.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces


Activepieces handles the work the helpdesk's own AI can't reach, such as steps that cross into other apps or wait on a person, across 750 integrations counted from its open source monorepo, with an MIT-licensed core. It doesn't replace the helpdesk.


### Where Activepieces fits and where it doesn't


Activepieces fits when the person who owns the support queue can describe the missing step in its built-in chat, say a billing lookup before a refund reply, and get a published flow back.


That flow is the same artifact an engineer would have assembled by hand, and it runs under the same RBAC, audit logs and run traces, so anyone can read what it did to a ticket. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


Its connectors are called pieces, and the pieces directory is where you check whether your helpdesk and your other tools are covered before you commit.


It doesn't fit when the helpdesk's own AI already does the job. In that case you're paying for, and maintaining, a second system that duplicates the first. If nobody on your team will own flows when they break, buy the helpdesk's automation and stop there.


### Worked workflow: triage a new ticket with approval


A draft never reaches a customer without a person's decision in between. That is the point of the flow below, which uses a new-ticket trigger, an AI step, a Slack message, an approval and a send action.


1. A new ticket arrives in the helpdesk and starts the flow.
2. An AI step classifies the ticket and drafts a reply.
3. A Slack message alerts the ticket's owner, with the category and the draft.
4. The owner approves or rejects the draft. The flow waits for that decision.
5. On approval, the reply is sent to the customer.


Step 4 is the one to inspect. If the flow has no path for a rejection or for an owner who never answers, the ticket sits silent, so build those branches before you switch it on.


Test each step against a real ticket and keep the run history open. A failed step shows up there, not in the customer's inbox.


### Pricing and self-hosting, checked on date


On the Activepieces pricing page, checked 2026-10-23, the Free plan is $0 with 1,000 credits a month, unlimited flows and up to 5 users, and Plus is $20 a month flat for 10,000 credits.


A run is 1 credit however many steps it has, while **AI steps cost more: 2 credits** on a fast model and 10 on a smart one.


Check what the billing unit is, which plans include approvals and access controls, and whether the self-hosted option covers what your security review requires. Self-hosting moves hosting and upgrades onto your staff, and you should count that as a cost.


Browse the[Activepieces pieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces) to confirm your apps are there, then start on the Free plan, which needs no card, and run the flow above on a test ticket.


Activepieces is the better fit for support leads who own the queue and need the steps their helpdesk's own AI can't reach, such as a billing lookup before a refund reply, without hiring an engineer to build them.


You describe the process in the built-in chat and get back a published flow in your account, with a run trace showing exactly what happened to each ticket, under the same RBAC and audit logs as a hand-built flow.


The helpdesk stays in place, and a reader whose stack falls outside the pieces directory should check coverage there before committing.
